sources.title: Continual Reinforcement Learning by Planning with Online World Models
sources.evidence: FTL shallow online world model + MPC; theoretical regret O(sqrt(K^2 D log T)); Continual Bench; abstract reports outperforming deep world-model continual-learning baselines without forgetting old skills.

sources.title: Replay can provably increase forgetting
sources.evidence: Forgetting can be non-monotonic in replay sample count; random replay can increase forgetting in expectation in specified linear-regression task families; neural-network SGD experiments show similar harmful-replay behavior; scope is task/subspace dependent.

sources.title: Revisiting Replay and Gradient Alignment for Continual Pre-Training of Large Language Models
sources.evidence: Llama-family continual pretraining across languages with 100B tokens per language. Replay and gradient alignment stabilize retention; small replay rates are reported as a better compute use than scaling model size, while high replay rates become less compute-efficient than scaling model size. Efficient MER adds gradient-alignment benefits with negligible stated compute/memory overhead.

sources.title: Using Partition-Tree Weighting and MAML for Continual and Online Learning
sources.evidence: Task-agnostic Switching-MNIST stream with unobserved stochastic context switches. Replay-MAML PTW uses PTW mixture/restarts plus an online replay-trained MAML initializer. At 100k steps: Replay-MAML PTW 97.5%±0.1 vs PTW 87.3%±0.3 and SGD 85.0%±0.3; it surpasses task-aware/offline MAML+SGD+Reset 96.5%±0.6. Replay-MAML SGD+Reset reaches 97.8%±0.0 at 100k. Buffer covers 1,250 timesteps (~25 tasks); method adds O(log T) compute/memory. In long-run experiments, all 30 plain-SGD trials collapse by 1M updates (earliest 92k), while PTW does not show the same catastrophic plasticity collapse.

sources.title: OASIS: Online Sample Selection for Continual Instruction Tuning
sources.evidence: Reference-model-free, inference-only adaptive sample selection using online global informativeness statistics plus redundancy reduction. On MICVIT with Qwen-VL-2.5-7B at 25% selection, Aavg 70.23±0.27 / Alast 76.41±0.41 vs full-data 72.31±0.42 / 78.18±0.75; best listed sampling baseline Aavg <=67.91 and Alast <=75.27. On LLaVA-1.5-7B MICVIT at 25%, OASIS 68.84±0.37 / 77.95±0.93 vs full 71.80±0.44 / 79.66±0.43. At 6.25%, OASIS 64.39±0.58 / 71.76±0.72 and is best among listed sampling methods. Paper states selection requires forward pass only and reports fewer FLOPs than gradient-based selection baselines.

sources.title: GRASP: A Rehearsal Policy for Efficient Online Continual Learning
sources.evidence: Easy/prototypical-first then progressively harder replay. Compared with 17 rehearsal policies, higher ImageNet CL accuracy; same performance as uniform balanced sampling with 40% fewer updates; also evaluated on five text classification datasets.

sources.title: Online Curvature-Aware Replay: Leveraging 2nd Order Information for Online Continual Learning
sources.evidence: Formulates replay OCL as constrained second-order online joint optimization; K-FAC/Fisher preconditioning stabilizes replay and accelerates non-interfering directions; reports higher average accuracy throughout training on three benchmarks.

sources.title: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Learning with Adaptive Linearity Injection
sources.evidence: Per-neuron learnable gating injects linearity based on gradient flow, without explicit task boundaries or reset hyperparameters; reports significant improvements across Random Label/Permuted MNIST, Random Label/Shuffled CIFAR-10, and Class-Split CIFAR-100; neuron-level adaptation is reported crucial in ablations.

sources.title: Reinitializing weights vs units for maintaining plasticity in neural networks
sources.evidence: Selective reinitialization of least-useful weights is more robust than unit reinitialization particularly in small networks and with layer normalization; weight and unit reinit are comparable in sufficiently wide non-LN networks.

sources.title: Beyond Cosine Decay: On the effectiveness of Infinite Learning Rate Schedule for Continual Pre-training
sources.evidence: Repeated cosine re-warming itself induces forgetting; infinite LR schedule improves continual pretraining across MAE and autoregressive LM settings. Reported MAE example: after all three tasks average accuracy 50.18%, about 1.3 points above repeated cosine; stronger retention after shifts, including 57.50% ImageNet accuracy under the stated strong shift.

sources.title: Continual Safety Alignment via Gradient-Based Sample Selection
sources.evidence: High-gradient samples cause greater safety/alignment drift; moderate-gradient samples retain task learning with less alignment loss. Filtering high-gradient samples improves alignment preservation across multiple model families and task orders without curated safe data or architecture changes. Exact metric table remains to be extracted next run.

sources.title: Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning
sources.evidence: Standard deep nets lose plasticity over extended nonstationary training; continual backprop reinitializing tiny fractions of low-utility units maintains diversity/plasticity across supervised and RL setups. Continual ImageNet early task accuracy can reach ~88%, but conventional backprop degrades strongly by task 2000; continual backprop maintains high stable rank and few dormant units.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Adaptive global online sample selection rather than fixed top-k per batch
candidate_mechanisms.why_it_matters: Three independent lines converge on selection quality over replay/sample quantity: OASIS tracks informativeness across the whole stream and removes redundancy; GRASP orders rehearsal easy-to-hard; harmful-replay theory shows more/random replay can worsen retention under some task geometries.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Strongest direct evidence for continual instruction tuning and image/text rehearsal; transfer to arbitrary continual agents requires validation.
candidate_mechanisms.confidence: high on selection principle; medium on cross-domain transfer

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Multi-timescale model mixture with learned online reset initialization
candidate_mechanisms.why_it_matters: Replay-MAML PTW combines multiple reset timescales with an online learned initializer, avoiding explicit task-boundary signals and outperforming a task-aware offline comparator in its benchmark. Long-run SGD collapse suggests reset/renewal is not only anti-forgetting but a plasticity-maintenance primitive.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Quantitative evidence is strong on Switching MNIST and qualitatively replicated on Fashion-MNIST/CIFAR-10; O(log T) mixture cost and classification-specific setup limit immediate generalization.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Plasticity-preserving parameter renewal targeted by utility/gradient flow
candidate_mechanisms.why_it_matters: Independent mechanisms (low-utility unit/weight reinit and adaptive linearization) support maintaining gradient flow/feature diversity throughout long streams rather than only replaying old data.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Primarily deep supervised/RL benchmarks; exact scaling to LLM continual training remains unresolved.
candidate_mechanisms.confidence: high that plasticity loss is real; medium on best mechanism for foundation models

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Low-rate replay + gradient alignment, not indiscriminate high replay
candidate_mechanisms.why_it_matters: Large-scale LLM evidence favors small replay rates and gradient alignment; theory warns random replay can be harmful; curvature-aware replay offers another way to protect old directions while allowing motion in non-interfering directions.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Exact optimal replay rate depends on data/task geometry and compute regime; do not generalize a single rate.
candidate_mechanisms.confidence: high on avoiding naive replay-volume monotonicity; medium on specific optimizer choice

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Schedule design as a retention mechanism: avoid repeated LR re-warm shocks
candidate_mechanisms.why_it_matters: For continual pretraining, optimization schedule alone can create forgetting; an infinite schedule removes fixed-budget/restart assumptions and improves retention in vision and language experiments.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Requires exact LM benchmark extraction and independent replication before strong recommendation.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Separate shared dynamics learning from task/reward adaptation via online world model + planning
candidate_mechanisms.why_it_matters: If tasks share dynamics, retaining a continually updated dynamics model while moving task specificity into reward-conditioned planning can structurally reduce destructive policy overwrite.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Applies specifically when tasks share state-space/dynamics or admit a useful shared model; needs quantitative table extraction before ranking against other candidates.

negative_and_boundary_evidence.claim: More replay is not monotonically better.
negative_and_boundary_evidence.scope: Proved in over-parameterized continual linear regression task families and supported by neural-network SGD/common benchmark experiments; not a universal claim that replay is harmful.

negative_and_boundary_evidence.claim: Plain SGD can catastrophically lose plasticity over long streams.
negative_and_boundary_evidence.scope: Replay-MAML PTW paper: earliest collapse 92k and all 30 Switching-MNIST trials by 1M updates; Nature 2024 gives broader supervised/RL evidence. This is distinct from catastrophic forgetting.

negative_and_boundary_evidence.claim: Full-data training is not automatically best under equal wall-clock adaptation constraints.
negative_and_boundary_evidence.scope: OASIS CIT experiments explicitly model training delay: full-data training can lag on newly arriving tasks; under unconstrained compute/full convergence this conclusion need not hold.

rejected_or_deprioritized_leads.lead: Sleep-like unsupervised replay / biological memory consolidation
rejected_or_deprioritized_leads.reason: Mechanistically interesting but strongest located ANN result is 2022 and the transfer path to current foundation-model continual training is less direct than newer benchmarked methods. Keep as a lower-priority mechanism branch, not a top candidate this run.

rejected_or_deprioritized_leads.lead: Curriculum-driven DQN expansion for train scheduling
rejected_or_deprioritized_leads.reason: Recent but strongly domain-specific multi-agent train-scheduling setup; weaker transfer evidence than GRASP/OASIS for general selection/curriculum principles.
